literal: Virtue it will yield, pleasure also it will yield, knowing the proper means, without evil, acquired wealth.
translation: Wealth that is acquired by knowing the proper means and without committing any evil will yield both virtue and pleasure.
modern: நல்வழியை அறிந்து, தீமை இல்லாமல் சேர்க்கப்பட்ட செல்வம், அறத்தையும் தரும்; இன்பத்தையும் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet explains the dual benefits of wealth that is acquired through righteous and proper means. When wealth is earned without causing harm or committing evil deeds (தீதின்றி), and by understanding the correct, ethical methods (திறனறிந்து), it becomes a source of true goodness. Such ethically earned wealth not only enables a person to perform virtuous deeds (அறன் ஈனும்) but also brings genuine happiness and pleasure (இன்பமும் ஈனும்) to their life. The poet emphasizes that the moral quality of how wealth is acquired directly determines its ultimate value and the joy it brings.
